entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8169"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 11</title> <div sID="gen12753" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.10">Ec 11:1-10</reference>.<div eID="gen12753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12754" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8169"/>1. <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference> shows that charity is here inculcated.<div eID="gen12754" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12755" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bread--</hi>bread corn. As in the Lord's prayer, all things needful for the body and soul. Solomon reverts to the sentiment (<reference osisRef="Eccl.9.10">Ec 9:10</reference>).<div eID="gen12755" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12756" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">waters--</hi>image from the custom of sowing seed by casting it from boats into the overflowing waters of the Nile, or in any marshy ground. When the waters receded, the grain in the alluvial soil sprang up (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.20">Is 32:20</reference>). "Waters" express multitudes, so <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.17.15">Re 17:15</reference>; also the seemingly hopeless character of the recipients of the charity; but it shall prove at last to have been not thrown away (<reference osisRef="Isa.49.4">Is 49:4</reference>). <div eID="gen12756" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 11 Ec 11:1-10 . 1. Ec 11:2 shows that charity is here inculcated. bread-- bread corn. As in the Lord's prayer, all things needful for the body and soul. Solomon reverts to the sentiment ( Ec 9:10 ). waters-- image from the custom of sowing seed by casting it from boats into the overflowing waters of the Nile, or in any marshy ground. When the waters receded, the grain in the alluvial soil sprang up ( Is 32:20 ). "Waters" express multitudes, so Ec 11:2 ; Re 17:15 ; also the seemingly hopeless character of the recipients of the charity; but it shall prove at last to have been not thrown away ( Is 49:4 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8170"/><div sID="gen12757" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8170"/><hi type="bold">2. portion--</hi>of thy bread.<div eID="gen12757" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12758" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seven--</hi>the perfect number.<div eID="gen12758" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12759" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eight--</hi>even to more than seven; that is, "to many" (so "waters," <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.1">Ec 11:1</reference>), nay, even to very many in need (<reference osisRef="Job.5.19">Job 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.5.5">Mi 5:5</reference>).<div eID="gen12759" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12760" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">evil--</hi>The day may be near, when you will need the help of those whom you have bound to you by kindnesses (<reference osisRef="Luke.16.9">Lu 16:9</reference>). The very argument which covetous men use against liberality (namely, that bad times may come), the wise man uses for it. <div eID="gen12760" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8171"/><div sID="gen12761" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8171"/><hi type="bold">3. clouds--</hi>answering to "evil" (<reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference>), meaning, When the times of evil are fully ripe, evil must come; and speculations about it beforehand, so as to prevent one sowing seed of liberality, are vain (<reference osisRef="Eccl.11.4">Ec 11:4</reference>).<div eID="gen12761" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12762" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tree--</hi>Once the storm uproots it, it lies either northward or southward, according as it fell. So man's character is unchangeable, whether for hell or heaven, once that death overtakes him (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.11">Re 22:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.15">14, 15</reference>). Now is his time for liberality, before the evil days come (<reference osisRef="Eccl.12.1">Ec 12:1</reference>). <div eID="gen12762" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 3. clouds-- answering to "evil" ( Ec 11:2 ), meaning, When the times of evil are fully ripe, evil must come; and speculations about it beforehand, so as to prevent one sowing seed of liberality, are vain ( Ec 11:4 ). tree-- Once the storm uproots it, it lies either northward or southward, according as it fell. So man's character is unchangeable, whether for hell or heaven, once that death overtakes him ( Re 22:11 , 14, 15 ). Now is his time for liberality, before the evil days come ( Ec 12:1 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8172"/><div sID="gen12763" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8172"/>4. Therefore sow thy charity in faith, without hesitancy or speculation as to results, because they may not seem promising (<reference osisRef="Eccl.9.10">Ec 9:10</reference>). So in <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.1">Ec 11:1</reference>, man is told to "cast his bread corn" on the seemingly unpromising "waters" (<reference osisRef="Ps.126.5">Psa 126:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.126.6">6</reference>). The farmer would get on badly, who, instead of sowing and reaping, spent his time in watching the wind and clouds. <div eID="gen12763" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4. Therefore sow thy charity in faith, without hesitancy or speculation as to results, because they may not seem promising ( Ec 9:10 ). The farmer would get on badly, who, instead of sowing and reaping, spent his time in watching the wind and clouds.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8176"/><div sID="gen12772" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8176"/>8. But while man thankfully enjoys life, "let him remember" it will not last for ever. The "many days of darkness," that is, the unseen world (<reference osisRef="Job.10.21">Job 10:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.10.22">22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.88.12">Psa 88:12</reference>), also days of "evil" in this world (<reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference>), are coming; therefore sow the good seed while life and good days last, which are not too long for accomplishing life's duties.<div eID="gen12772" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12773" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">All that cometh--</hi>that is, All that followeth in the evil and dark days is vain, as far as work for God is concerned (<reference osisRef="Eccl.9.10">Ec 9:10</reference>). <div eID="gen12773" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 8. But while man thankfully enjoys life, "let him remember" it will not last for ever. The "many days of darkness," that is, the unseen world ( Job 10:21 , 22 ; Psa 88:12 ), also days of "evil" in this world ( Ec 11:2 ), are coming; therefore sow the good seed while life and good days last, which are not too long for accomplishing life's duties. All that cometh-- that is, All that followeth in the evil and dark days is vain, as far as work for God is concerned ( Ec 9:10 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8177"/><div sID="gen12774" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8177"/><hi type="bold">9. Rejoice--</hi>not advice, but warning. So <reference osisRef="1Kgs.22.15">1Ki 22:15</reference>, is irony; if thou dost rejoice (carnally, <reference osisRef="Eccl.2.2">Ec 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.7.2">7:2</reference>, not moderately, as in <reference osisRef="Eccl.5.18">Ec 5:18</reference>), &c., then "know that ... God will bring thee into judgment" (<reference osisRef="Eccl.3.17">Ec 3:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.12.14">12:14</reference>).<div eID="gen12774" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12775" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">youth ... youth--</hi>distinct Hebrew words, adolescence or boyhood (before <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.10">Ec 11:10</reference>), and full-grown youth. It marks the gradual progress in self-indulgence, to which the young especially are prone; they see the roses, but do not discover the thorns, until pierced by them. Religion will cost self-denial, but the want of it infinitely more (<reference osisRef="Luke.14.28">Lu 14:28</reference>). <div eID="gen12775" type="x-p"/>
